articleTitle: Automatic calibration methodology using machine learning with low-cost and meteorological sensors
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: In the last years several low-cost sensors (LCS) were installed in Lima, however, the accuracy, reliability, comparability and standardization compared with robust Senamhi sensors is a problem. The calibration helps to align the readings of the LCS with the known reference concentration sensors and values, on the other hand the reliability helps to reduce the variations in readings caused by factors like temperature changes, humidity and sensor degradation; besides, the comparability allows to compare the data across different monitoring systems with the standardization making it easier to interpret and compare data registered from different LCS. Therefore, an evaluation of LCS and Senamhi sensors with several algorithms were tested with five algorithms; for the calibration of the PM2.5 with EPA standards set limits for the concentration of fine particles with the calibration of the sensors with Random Forest, in the air with the highest value of correlation with 91.92%, with MAE 2.462 µ g/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, RAE of 35.7328%, and RRSE of 49.0361%.

articleTitle: Mechatronics Design of Wheeled Mobile Robotic System for Gutter Maintenance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: This paper deals with the challenges involved on roof building gutter maintenance robot design, from the problem statement of secure teleoperated semiautonomous navigation on confined gutter spaces, and the best selection of right mechatronics brush to remove the waste on gutter surface; Two concept design have been tested: Passive Brush with Parallel locomotion (PBP), and Active Brush Axial (ABA). The results on our development are shown, as following: secure robot lifting regulation, simulation environment, HMI to teleoperate, mechatronics design. Finally, some tests on simulations and current prototypes are shown, to validate our proposal, and the conclusion that the ABA design allows to remove until 85% gutter waste, instead of PBP design; furthermore, the ABA allows independent brush rotation velocity, instead of PBP design.

articleTitle: 3-D Electric Fields and Induced Potentials inside High-Voltage Air Insulated Substation Switchyards
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: This work presents a state-of-the-art formulation to calculate Electric Fields and Induced Potentials in Air Insulated Substation (AIS) switchyards generated by energized busbars at 50/60-Hz. A computer algorithm based on the Charge Simulation Method (CSM) and the Method of Images is developed. Electric Field 3-D distributions and Induced Potentials considering grounded and ungrounded steel-framework structures are calculated for a 230 kV AIS switchyard using basic geometric and electric parameters as initial data. Procedure accuracy is verified by comparing Electric Field 2-D profiles with those calculated by Finite Element Method (FEM). Induced Potentials in steel-framework structures grounded, ungrounded and grounded through a high substation grounding resistance are assessed.

articleTitle: On the Use of Open Air Interface and OpenBTS for Mobile Communications Education in Telecommunications Laboratories
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: Telecommunications engineering plays a fundamental role in supporting mobile networks that have undergone rapid evolution and technological improvements in recent decades, both in network components and their application in various vertical industries. Indeed, telecommunications engineers are responsible for designing, implementing, optimizing, and maintaining mobile network infrastructures to ensure their efficient and reliable operation. To ensure proper preparation of electronic and telecommunications engineering students, it is essential for them to acquire theoretical knowledge and practical experience in the operation and evaluation of mobile network components. In this regard, this article proposes the use of simulators and emulators as a more flexible and cost-effective alternative for the development of 2G, 4G, and 5G NSA mobile networks. Specifically, the use of open-source software such as OpenBTS and Open Air Interface is suggested, which allows for the implementation of mobile networks using software-defined radio (SDR) modules. Additionally, a list of laboratory experiences that can be conducted with the implemented systems is proposed.

articleTitle: A design and analysis of a Darrieus Helical vertical axis wind generator by numerical simulation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: This study addresses the problem of pollution and high energy demand in Peru, caused by population growth in the city. It proposes the use of renewable energy as a solution and seeks to analyze and design a vertical-axis wind turbine (VAWT) with variable rotor radius to evaluate its sustainability in Piura, Peru, as a renewable energy option. Climatological data from the Global Wind Atlas and the Capitán FAP Víctor Montes Arias Airport in Talara, Piura, were used. The blades were designed with aerodynamic models from SANDIA laboratories and analyzed using simulation software such as QBLADE and ANSYS FLUENT. The results indicate that the VAWT is efficient (Cp = 0.58) when the blades are contracted at 13.4 m/s. A closed-loop control is proposed to adjust the rotor radius with an anemometer. In addition, the airfoil behavior is observed by pressure and velocity plots in ANSYS FLUENT.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-based Segmentation and Classification System for Artichoke Seedling Grading
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: This study introduces a strategy for the automated grading of artichoke seedlings, a critical task in the transplantation process. The proposed strategy leverages two distinct perspectives, vertical and horizontal, to capture images of the seedlings using depth cameras. These images are then processed through segmentation modules to extract specific morphological attributes such as width, height, and leaf area. A feature vector composed of these attributes is evaluated by a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) to classify the seedlings into two categories: ‘good’ and ‘not good’. Two deep learning models, Mask R-CNN and YOLOv8, were employed for detection and instance segmentation tasks. Various backbones were experimented with, and the most effective ones were identified for both models. An MLP was developed for the classification stage, achieving an accuracy of 85.19% with specific training parameters. This research contributes a foundational framework for automated seedling grading, with potential applications and improvements in the field of agricultural automation.

articleTitle: Artificial vision strategy for Ripeness assessment of Blueberries on Images taken during Pre-harvest stage in Agroindustrial Environments using Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: This article introduces a methodology aimed at detecting and categorizing blueberries within an agro-industrial farm. The methodology employs a combination of YOLOv8 and a custom convolutional neural network. The process initiates with the creation of a dataset used for training and validating the proposed approach. Subsequently, the manual generation of masks for blueberries in the captured images is carried out, ensuring precise labeling that corresponds to five distinct ripeness levels. A model is developed to detect and classify the blueberries based on their respective ripeness levels. The evaluation of these models demonstrates a notable accuracy of 91.14% in the task of classifying the blueberries.

articleTitle: Performance of a new direct mechanical drive PTO for a hinged arm wave energy converter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: Ocean waves contain the highest energy density among renewable energy sources. However, the harnessing from ocean waves represents a challenge because the wave energy converter must be designed to show great survivability and efficiency. The power production challenge of any wave energy converter depends on the efficiency of the power take-off system. The direct mechanical drive power take-off system is one of the most efficient, the gearbox represents a necessary component in this power take-off system to increase the power generation. This study aims to address the analysis of power performance of a new wave energy converter composed of a point absorber, a hinged arm, and a direct mechanical drive power take-off system. The power take-off is characterized by a pulley system, one-way bearings, a gearbox, a flywheel, and an electric generator, in the present study it is considered a cylindrical point absorber. A wave-to-wire model is developed to simulate the coupled hydro-electro-mechanical system in regular waves. The study shows that the gear ratio is a parameter that greatly influences power generation. The mean power of the wave energy converter is high at low values of wave period and at high values of wave height.

articleTitle: Communication of Earthquake Warning Systems Through the RDS Standard Using the CAP-PER Protocol in Building Health Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: The alert dissemination time of a seismic alert system allows evaluating the efficiency in alerting the population in a short time. In this research, a seismic alert system was proposed to generate an alert message automatically according to the vibration level of the P wave in a building when an earthquake occurs. This system is composed to an Internet-FM communication system, servers and acquisition and activation modules. The results show that the seismic alert system has a rapid response, less than or equal to 600 ms, to a seismic event of any of the intensity levels analyzed with a probability of 86.9%.

articleTitle: Yolo algorithms to improve the detection of personal protective equipment thought industrial computer vision
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: During 2023, accidents at work are unexpected situations that cause losses in both human and material resources. In Peru there is current legislation that encourages a safe work environment, however, according to 2019 reports from the Ministry of Labor and Employment Promotion, 31.92% of accidents caused this year directly affected the cranial area. The use of personal protective equipment requires finding an optical way to identify the required safety equipment in real time. In response to this problem, the use of artificial vision or computer vision for helmet recognition. The trained model for online personal protective equipment classifier algorithms with computer vision in industrial applications allows to detect helmets, head, safety glasses, industrial vests with precision metrics greater than 88% according to light intensity. Additionally, it is possible to improve the accuracy of the other clusters by training with higher epochs, increasing batch processing from eight to sixteen, and using parallel processing. Despite the fact that the configuration profile for the training process carried out was basic, the database used, due to the varied labeling and number of images, acceptable results were obtained. Also, due to the selection of the YOLOV5m model, transfer learning training contributed to the training time without reducing the accuracy rates. Our findings is the recognition of a model with 5000 pictures with an accuracy of 88% from 400 to 800 lux and limited for the light intensity lower than 400 lux, with 78.63%. With light intensity higher than 800 lux, the recognition time of less than 0.3 seconds/image together with a rate of 98% with a low-cost camera and parallel processing with a Raspberry Pi version 4.

articleTitle: Security Evaluation of Open Access Wi-Fi Networks in a Public University in Junin, Peru
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: This article develops a topic of interest for users who can access the Internet and do not know the dangers of connecting to a free access network where the administrator of this is unknown, so a connection to this network would not be recommended. The central theme of this research is to demonstrate the risks of connecting to unknown access networks. The methodology used was the evaluation of how many users were being connected to the network created to monitor. The data obtained from users already connected have also been evaluated. According to the days they were connected through the networks, there is a strong demand for connected users. The conclusions show that some users are unaware of the dangers of connecting to one of these networks mentioned above and the risk of the amount of information that a person connected to the same network can obtain with the help of programs already created for its correct use. This work is a product of evaluating the dangers of connecting to an unknown network in Huancayo, Peru.

articleTitle: NoHateS: A Transformers-based Approach for Real-Time Hate Speech Detection in Spanish
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: Hate speech detection is a challenging task, especially in the context of real-time monitoring on the internet. Manual detection is both exhausting and impractical due to the high volume and frequency of online data. This paper proposes a system called NoHateS. This system is made of multiple components, the main one is BETO-CNN, a Transformers-based model trained on a Spanish corpus, which is designed to actually detect whether a text contains hate speech or not. The second component is developed to ensure accessibility. This includes an API to allow seamless integration of the model into various applications, and a Discord Bot developed for easy manipulation of the aforementioned API in order to help users detect hate speech in text channels. This paper also includes tests with imbalanced data and applies data augmentation in order to deal with it and make more robust models. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of NoHateS in detecting hate speech and provide recommendations for future research in this domain as it achieves 72.63% and 72.94% F1-score on the non-augmented and augmented dataset respectively.

articleTitle: Modular boards to reduce exercise implementation time in MCU classes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: Hardware implementation in a microcontroller class is important for the academic training of engineering students because it allows the use of the theory and programming codes developed in an MCU class. The implementation allows students to understand the interaction of the MCU with other components that enable the development of a project. This research aims to design and implement a set of modular cards to reduce the implementation time of exercises developed in a MCU class at the Universidad Tecnológica del Perú (UTP). Therefore, the design of cards under a modular approach is performed, in addition, a user interface (UI) containing the necessary information for the use of the cards is designed and executed. Subsequently, a series of pre-tests and post-tests are carried out with UTP students to obtain implementation times. The results indicate that the use of the modular cards and the UI allows the student to save implementation time. Finally, a survey is conducted with engineering students regarding the cards and UI.

articleTitle: Underground XLPE mathematical model for medium voltage
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: This paper demonstrates a mathematical model for underground XLPE cable and the limitations of current international standards regarding the number of cables allowed in a single trench and explores key aspects that should be considered in future designs. The mathematical modelling improves the process from the international standards IEC 60287, 60502, and 60228. In these standards, the quantity of underground cables is two in the same trench. However, with the proposed methodology, the quantity could increase according to the necessary quantity of cables. Our findings are the equations and factors for the application of one to five circuits in the same trench and the considerations of several trenches in parallel to represent the thermal degradation and the maximum current, validated with finite element analysis for all the case study. This research article provides valuable insights into the challenges associated with medium voltage underground cable design to include in the future of the international standard to increase the cable quantity in the trench; according to the model and the validation, the accuracy of process has the following accuracy for 240mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>: 99.4850± 0.5150 %; and for 630mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> has an accuracy of 99.3698±0.6301 %.

articleTitle: Methodology for the design of large wind farms
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: The wind farms are spreading around the world, however, the optimization of the layout is a challenge caused by turbulence and wind velocity for large scale projects. In this paper, it evaluates the result of the Components, Environmental, Structure and Modelling (CESM) methodology with a complete mathematical modelling. Our findings are an optimized design improved yearly energy production by 197% compared with the optimized traditional design of 122% with the turbulence influence.

articleTitle: Generalized Predictive Control for Speed Regulation in Three-Phase Induction Motors: Design and Validation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: This research highlights the relevance of the Generalized Predictive Control (GPC) Controller for speed control of induction motors in modern industry. GPC is an advanced technique that uses mathematical models and predictive techniques to achieve accurate and efficient motor speed control. A GPC controller is implemented in conjunction with a parallel PI using Python, a programming language widely used in scientific and control applications. The choice of Python is justified by its flexibility, ease of development and access to specialised libraries, such as NumPy, which facilitate the manipulation of matrices and the implementation of advanced control algorithms.

articleTitle: Robotic Pollination System for Chirimoya Plantations in the Huánuco Region
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: In this research article, the design of a semiautomatic Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) is proposed for the detection of chirimoya flowers and artificial pollination to increase chirimoya fruit production. The UAV will fly through chirimoya trees and will be equipped with sensors and actuators to identify flowers on the branches and activate the robotic pollination system. The design of the robotic arm, fuselage, and mechanical resistance simulations are developed, and a general description is provided of what is expected to be developed, including the electrical and electronic components. The results section focuses on validating the mechanical strength of the fuselage and the robotic arm, as well as the dynamic simulation of the latter using MATLAB, which completes the pollination task.

articleTitle: Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) Control for the Active Suspension System of a Four-Wheeled Agricultural Robot
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: As the adoption of robotics within the agricultural industry increases, the issue of maintaining stability and precise task execution on irregular terrain has emerged as a critical challenge. To address this, this study introduces a control strategy for enhancing the suspension system of an agricultural mobile robot. A dynamic model, characterized in the state-space representation, was formulated to encapsulate the robot’s suspension dynamics. This model was then interfaced with a Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) for optimized control. Performance evaluations were conducted using MATLAB/Simulink, and two contrasting road profiles were employed to simulate agricultural terrains. When compared to the passive counterpart, the active LQR-controlled suspension presented substantial improvements. Specifically, for the initial road profile, the roll angle, pitch angle, and vertical acceleration showed improvements of 40.68%, 39.47%, and 37.73%, respectively. On the second road profile characterized by depressions, these metrics improved by 52.02%, 66.97%, and 71.03%. Consequently, the proposed LQR control strategy enhances the robot’s stability and precision on challenging agricultural terrains by reducing oscillations and minimizing stabilization time.

articleTitle: Energy Period and Multimodality of Sea Spectra in the Peru Basin
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: Assessing the wave energy resource in zones without spectral data leads to assumptions based on theory to estimate wave parameters such as the energy period. The energy period has been regularly approximated using a calibration coefficient based on a standard spectral shape such as the Bretschneider spectrum—representing a single-mode sea state—and the zero-up-crossing period. As a result, assessments of wave energy resources that rely on this practice are only accurate if the spectral shape is single-mode. This work uses spectral data provided by an ocean buoy in the Peru Basin. We presented an algorithm based on comprehensive criteria used in this field to find how many modes the spectrum exhibits. Also, the characteristic periods are estimated using the spectral method in the frequency domain. It is important to study the configuration of maximum energy, or multimodal spectrum, to find the more accurate calibration coefficient or relationship between the energy period and the zero-up-crossing period to estimate the wave power precisely. This procedure, in turn, is important for increasing the reliability of harnessing the wave energy resource through wave energy converters. As the Peru Basin is an open maritime zone, the calibration coefficient may present increased differences in combined sea states with two maximum energy or two modes. The number of modes in the sea spectra should partially explain increased differences in the calibration coefficient. This work aims to find any influence that the presence of multiple modes in the sea spectra has on the calibration coefficient. In conclusion, the sea spectra in the Peru Basin have up to four modes with different behaviours on a monthly time scale. The single or bi-modal spectra exhibit no erratic behaviour. The calibration coefficient’s average for one and two modes ranges from 1.3 up to 1.4 throughout the year. The calibration coefficient for single and bi-modal spectra decreases gradually for the most energetic months and then increases gradually for the less energetic months. As this calibration coefficient is significant to estimate the wave power precisely, using a global average but specific values for each month is not recommended.

articleTitle: Genetic-Algorithm-Based Tuning of PID Controllers for a Multipurpose Water Tank Plant
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: PID controllers for industrial processes have been usually tuned by methods such as Ziegler-Nichols, Cohen-Coon, frequency-based, root-locus-based and many others. Metaheuristic methods including genetic algorithms can optimize parameters to minimize cost functions, thus these techniques can be also used to tune PID controllers. The present study focuses on the design of PID controllers tuned by a simplified genetic algorithm for a multipurpose water tank plant in Peru, in order to optimize the parameters and improve its performance for single-loop and multi-loop control. For this purpose, the experimentally obtained transfer functions of the industrial multi-input multi-output plant are utilized, and a simplified genetic algorithm is proposed. It is demonstrated that in most of the cases, the PID gains obtained by the genetic algorithm compared to pid-tune tool of Matlab is superior according to the performance indexes in flow, pressure, level and temperature loops.

articleTitle: Prototype Peltier Cell Air Conditioning Using Photovoltaic Energy
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: The demand for air conditioning systems has experienced a significant increase due to rising global temperatures, urbanization, and improved living standards, especially in regions of Peru where summer is intense, and temperatures tend to range between 25°C-31C°. However, this increase presents challenges related to energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions. Therefore, the development of more efficient and sustainable technologies is required. This article seeks to provide a self-sustainable, economical, and efficient solution to reduce temperatures in rooms, homes, buildings, and other structures using thermoelectric panels (TEACs) and photovoltaic energy.

articleTitle: Effects of using NFPA 780 maximum installation distances to configure air-termination systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: In this work, we study the effects of using only the maximum installation distances of air terminals endorsed by NFPA 780 to validate or configure separation distances in air-termination systems. The protected zone of single and multiple air terminals is assessed through a case evaluation example by employing the 3-D Rolling Sphere Method approach along with simplified formulae provided herein for practical analysis. We propose curves for in-field validation of the maximum height of protected structures for NFPA 780 maximum air terminal distances, considering air terminal lengths of 0,30 m and 0,60 m, and their location near the corners, edges and inner rooftop.

articleTitle: Temporal Variability of the Sea Spectrum in the Peru Basin
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: The current shortcoming in the development of wave energy technology is the shortage of available ocean data. To manage the lack of ocean data, theoretical assumptions are usually considered. These reasonable assumptions like adopting a standard spectrum have been applied in many wave energy resource assessments. These assessments relied on a specific standard spectrum like JONSWAP or Bretschneider to model wave parameters. However, the shape of these theoretical spectra is characterised by a single peak. As the Peru Basin is an open maritime zone mostly without islands, there should be significant spectral shape variability due to several wave systems like swells and wind waves, making its spectral shape not present a single peak. Thus, this particular spectral shape should represent the sea states in the Peru Basin more accurately than the standard spectra. This work aims to demonstrate that the spectral shape in the Peru Basin has significant variability throughout the year and according to the distribution of the classes of annual energy contribution. This work uses spectral data provided by ocean buoys in the Peru Basin. The wave parameters are modelled using the spectral method and assuming the standard Bretschneider spectrum, which only considers one wave system, to represent the open maritime zone. These results then contrast with the actual average spectral shape of the Peru Basin. The paper concludes that the Peru Basin’s spectral shape only partially matches the regularly used Bretschneider spectrum—the spectral shape changes during the year from single to bimodal. The spectral shape also changes according to the classes of energy period and significant wave height, having one or two energy modes or wave systems. Thus, the peak period is far correlated to the zero-up-crossing period, and its actual relationship does not follow the theoretical assumption based on the Bretschneider spectrum. It is important to study the actual spectral shape variability and compare its shape against standard spectra to verify their agreement. This study is crucial for designing wave energy converters, which are regularly designed based on standard spectra.

articleTitle: A system for detecting objects and estimating their distance using a neural network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: This article proposes using neural networks to solve the challenge of accurately measuring the distance of an object using cameras and digital image processing. For this, a neural network was trained using a data set that includes information on the distance in pixels of the centers of mass of the object detected by the cameras. This data was used to teach the network to make an accurate estimate of the actual distance of the object. Image analysis methods were also used in conjunction with images of the object previously captured and trained with YoloV8 on Roboflow. The results obtained showed a notable improvement in the precision that is obtained when measuring the distance without the tedious calibration that is had in the other approaches considered for this investigation. Overcame the challenges associated with camera calibration due to possible distortion, accuracy, and generalization generated by changing the environment, resulting in an effective solution with 90% accuracy percentage and a dense neural network with an input layer, a hidden layer and an output layer with 2000 training cycles. These results demonstrate the potential of neural networks and image processing to address distance measurement problems in various applications, such as robotics, road safety, and autonomous navigation.

articleTitle: Maturity model for data leakage security protocols in telecommunications companies applying the NIST framework
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: Attacks on information security and data leaks in telecommunications companies in Peru cause considerable losses both financially and in terms of social reputation. For this reason, response protocols have been implemented to deal with these situations. However, the mere implementation and development of these protocols is not enough to effectively prevent or counter attacks. Therefore, a technological solution is proposed that combines a maturity assessment model for protocols and a reporting system that provides information on the current level and possible improvements that can be applied to the assessed protocols. The project aims to reduce attacks on companies in the telecommunications sector and at the same time enable them to assess the state of their protocols in terms of cybersecurity, giving them greater insight into possible situations that could result from protocol misuse. To validate the project, 4 cybersecurity experts were involved, who have used it for a given period to obtain sufficient information to offer their opinion. At the end of the period of use, a form was sent to them to evaluate the level of satisfaction with the project, using the indicators that were established. The final level of satisfaction obtained was 81.39%, which indicates that the project has been successful according to the evaluation of the security experts.

articleTitle: Maqya: Design of an autonomous low cost beach-cleaner robot for endanger beaches
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: Pollution is a frequent problem on the most crowded beaches in cities. To solve this problem, the design of a robot integrated with computer vision that identifies places affected by excess waste is proposed and through the mechanical system, the collection of these is carried out for subsequent disposal. Hence, we have developed a low-cost autonomous cleaner robot design that using a YOLO V8 architecture will detect garbage on the sand beach in order to collect them. As a result, the robot was simulated using Robot Operating System (ROS) framework, and the predictive model with the best performance got a 90.95% precision, 78.37% recall, and an F1-Score of 84.19%, using the TACO dataset to train it.

articleTitle: Trap camera prototype with remote monitoring system through LoRa technology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: Camera traps are widely used in the observation of wild animals in their natural habitat. Since these cameras must be installed seeking not to alter the habitat, their installation and maintenance are usually crucial, and their manipulation must be minimal. One of the risks of its use is the lack of knowledge of the battery status and the memory availability of images. Considering that the work environment usually lacks commercial wireless communication networks and that the equipment works with batteries, this work presents the development of a camera trap with remote wireless sending of the battery and memory status. The design considers different strategies for low energy consumption in a Raspberry board and the use of LoRa technology to send data.

articleTitle: Proposal for the Implementation of a Web Platform to Reinforce the Learning of the Mathematical Reasoning Course for Sixth Grade of Primary School
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: Currently, the traditional teaching methodology used in educational centers is not effectively adapted to the current technological era, which can lead to poor academic performance of students, especially in the subject of mathematical reasoning. The objective of the research is to develop a web platform that reinforces the learning of mathematical reasoning in sixth grade students. For this purpose, the agile software development methodology SCRUM was used, due to its agility and flexibility in the development process. In addition, the Game Learning methodology was used for the development of the web page content. The results obtained by conducting the experiment through a control and experimental group, in addition to the application of a survey, obtained a Spearman’s Rho of 0.891 and a significance of less than 0.05, demonstrating that there is a relationship between the use of the web platform and the learning of mathematical reasoning. Thus, it is demonstrated that the use of ICT (information and communication technologies) benefits students, since it improves in several aspects in relation to traditional teaching, as evidenced in the experiment an improvement of 3.331% of the experimental group compared to the control group. Therefore, it is plausible to conclude that the use of a web platform accompanied by the Game Learning methodology reinforces students’ learning in general.

articleTitle: Neural Rendering in the Cloud with Tensor Processing Unit
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: Neural Rendering, an intersection of computer graphics techniques and machine learning, has a significant impact on the generation of hyperrealistic content. This research advocates for the application of scalable, cloud-based digitization techniques within the realms of academia and culture to create sustainable models that can be efficiently preserved in minimal storage spaces, using on-demand free resources. This work introduces a Scalable Cloud-based Neural Rendering Prototype System (NRPS) powered by TPUs, made possible by the TPU Research Cloud (TRC) program. It was evaluated across three distinct architectures: (1) TPU VM, (2) TPU Node, and (3) TPU Node with GKE. The performance of the NRPS was assessed using images from the cultural heritage of Puno. The results demonstrate that the NRPS functions efficiently when employing TPUs in a scalable manner while minimizing CPU and RAM costs, particularly when utilizing the TPU Node architecture with GKE. The TPU Node architecture with GKE showcased superior scalability while requiring minimal VM resources, albeit with a 50% reduction in production capacity and a 120% increase in processing time, resulting in a daily production capacity of 1440 models. This research concludes that the TPU VM architecture is suitable for experimental production or scenarios requiring quick access to results, whereas the TPU Node with GKE is well-suited for scalable production. Furthermore, this work highlights the untapped potential of emerging technologies in enhancing academic research and cultural preservation, with a focus on efficiency and sustainability.

articleTitle: Grid-connected solar inverter capable of not returning electricity to the single-phase grid by controlling the power point of the PV panels
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: This article presents a grid-connected high-frequency solar inverter capable of operating in countries where their electric infrastructure or electric normative framework does not allow solar photovoltaic (PV) micro-generation in urban environments. The proposed inverter is based on an isolated single-state Dual - Active - Bridge Series - Resonant (DABSR) DC/AC converter. Unlike other DABSR structures, a full-wave Cycloconvert is used in the topology to convert the high-frequency AC into the desired line-frequency AC output without the necessity of unfolding bridges. The phase shift modulation strategy is applied to control the power flow. A modified version of the conventional Perturb and Observe (P&O) Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) algorithm is developed to ensure an instantaneous self-consumption with zero injection to the electricity grid. Finally, simulations are shown to verify the functionality of the inverter.

articleTitle: Kinematic Modeling of a Mobile Robot with Four Tractor-Type Wheels with Independent Electric Drive
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: The kinematic model of a mobile robot provides a mathematical description of the robot's motion, which is essential for controlling its movement. Since, by knowing the relationship between the speed of the wheels and the motion of the robot, a controller can be designed to allow the robot to follow a desired trajectory or avoid obstacles. In addition, it allows simulation of its motion in different scenarios, which is useful for testing and optimizing the design of the mobile robot, improving its stability and maneuverability. The latter is important for mobile robot applications in agricultural fields, given the irregularities of the terrain, and even more so if these applications are of the autonomous navigation type. In this work, the kinematics of a mobile robot of 110 cm wide, 140 cm long, and 40 cm high is modeled in order to have the model of the robot to be controlled for trajectory tracking. First, several kinematic modeling approaches are analyzed and studied to determine the one that best describes the motion of a particular robot. Second, the previously selected kinematic technique is applied to obtain the mathematical motion model of the particular robot. Finally, several results and discussions of the simulation are presented.

articleTitle: New fractals as images of classic fractals under a complex polynomial transformation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: This paper proposes a new way of generating fractal sets using classic fractal sets and complex polynomial transformations. This study maps a classic fractal using a complex polynomial transformation, giving rise to a new fractal set. It is important to note that from a classic fractal, you can obtain different images that have the behavior of a fractal set, depending on the transformation used. The box count dimension method shows that the new images can be located within the Fractal Geometry since they are dimensioned fractional. This proposal generates a new class of fractal sets and opens up the possibility of new applications, considering the applications offered by classic fractal sets.

articleTitle: Analysis of Induced Voltages on the Sheath of Double-Circuit Underground Power Lines - Part I: Without Phases Transposition
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: This paper introduces mathematical formulations for calculating induced voltages on the sheath of non-transposed double-circuit underground transmission lines, emphasizing four formations of three-phase power lines. For these formations, sectionalized and continuous cross-bonding techniques were employed to evaluate and reduce induced voltages on sheath. Our study centers on two critical aspects: first, calculating induced voltages on the sheath of underground lines and, subsequently, computing current imbalance in an underground sub-transmission system. The results indicate that the induced voltages and currents on the sheath generated by the four formations are distinct in each phase, uncontrolled, and have high values. The induced voltages achieved values up to 287.88 V when utilizing the flat formation with continuous cross-bonding, leading to high losses on the sheath and decreasing the current rating. This comparative study emphasizes the importance of carefully evaluating the method of bonding the sheaths, the types of formations used, and the necessity of phases transposition to ensure the safe and efficient operation of double-circuit underground transmission lines.

articleTitle: Analysis of Induced Voltages on the Sheath of Double-Circuit Underground Power Lines - Part II: With Phases Transposition
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: This paper presents mathematical formulations for calculating induced voltages on the sheath of double-circuit underground transmission lines, focusing on four formations involving phases of transposition. The study analyzes the application of sectionalized and continuous cross-bonding techniques to assess and reduce induced voltages. Two crucial aspects are assessed: calculating induced voltages on the sheath of underground lines and computing current imbalance in an underground sub-transmission system. The findings demonstrate that utilizing phases transposition allows for effective control and reduced induced voltage on the sheath. However, in practical scenarios, a residual induced voltage persists due to minor section length variations, resulting in low losses on the sheath. Notably, the flat formation exhibits the highest residual induced voltage among all formations, reaching up to 12.69 V with continuous cross-bonding. Nevertheless, this still results in relatively low losses on the sheath. The study underscores the critical role of phases transposition in ensuring double-circuit underground transmission lines’ safe and efficient operation. Additionally, the study reveals that whether phases transposition is implemented or not has no direct influence on the imbalance of the sub-transmission system current. This emphasizes the significance of carefully considering the choice of formations and cross-bonding techniques to achieve optimal performance and reliability in the transmission network.

articleTitle: Systems Review: The Role of Light Spectrum in Plant Productivity and Quality in Vertical Farming Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: The evolution of agriculture towards agricultural innovation, especially in the case of vertical farming (VF), a competitive system for sustainable food production, determines that light is a crucial factor in vertical farming. The substitution of sunlight with artificial light, mainly through LED lighting, has improved productivity. There has been exponential growth in the use of VF systems, but there needs to be more analysis and information on the research conducted in this field. To remediate this gap, a bibliometric review of 120 scientific articles from the SCOPUS database uses information from 79 articles published in relevant journals. In recent years, publications on VF systems have increased by 195%, with China developing most experiments in this field. Lettuce cultivation is the most predominant in these investigations, with a light intensity of 200 μmol•m−2•s−1 and a photoperiod of 16 h•day−1, using blue and red light spectra, The use of vertical farming for fresh and local produce has increased in recent years; Thus, many researchers demonstrated in their experiments that VF is going to be highly effective in productivity and quality. The conditions and management of VF systems have become standardized, with over 50% of the research using similar photoperiod, spectrum, and intensity methods. Vertical farming is considered a potentially sustainable and controllable means that can be developed in urban areas, benefiting the social economy, food security, and the environment. However, there are still open and improving aspects, such as resource utilization percentage, including alternative energy for system development.

articleTitle: Design methodology for heat transfer system with low-cost perspective
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: This paper develops an analysis of the performance and feasibility of an absorption refrigeration system powered by biogas as a source of heat generation applied to a quail farm. For this, an exhaustive review was carried out highlighting similar configurations of several generation sources, to obtain a better panorama when using biogas as a source for heat generation and achieve an equal better fit to a referential coefficient of operation (COP) of 0.1 to 0.13 of the proposed system based on the reviews presented considering the cooling of the environment between 20°C and 25°C. The findings are a lithium bromide solution, it was adequate for the operation of the system due to its great absorption capacity as indicated by its coefficient of performance (0.6 - 1.4). The thermodynamic analysis for the design of this proposed refrigeration system has been carried out, considering the parameters and flow points, temperature, pressure, etc. A COP of 0.8294 is obtained and the thermodynamic analysis, the volumetric consumption of biogas increases in the concentrator and/or burner of the heat generator, the power generated as the burner temperature increases and finally the increase in temperature depending on the volumetric consumption of biogas.

articleTitle: Mobile application for interactive learning of human anatomy using augmented reality
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: In the last decade, the push for digitalization due to the recent pandemic has led to the constant evolution of different fields. However, in the field of anatomy education, students' learning resources remain the same as they have been used in recent years, as does the lack of technological skills among educators in Peru. With the aim of providing a new alternative for learning human anatomy to the general public and promoting technology, the project aims to design, implement and validate a mobile application solution using augmented reality. This innovative approach helps to address a potential impact on the quality of education in the country. Our research demonstrates the feasibility and benefits of integrating AR into anatomy education such as improved enthusiasm for learning and retention of information versus traditional methods. All of this is reflected in the enhancement of comprehension and educational outcomes.

articleTitle: Systematic Review for the analysis of the business plan of the integral center for the Peruvian army
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: This research article develops a deep systematic review to create a business plan for the implementation of a integral center for the Peruvian army, in this case, the methodology applied is the meta-heuristic method called PICOC, it allows to identify the relevant papers for the main contribution, limitations and key performance indicators (KPIs); with the variables for the analysis, model recommended and the instrument for the implementation of the business plan, with the evaluation of the Equality, timely dedication, adequate infrastructure, lifestyle, comprehensive care center, quality of life and the dimensions of emotional well-being, behavior of the elderly and physical well-being; with a deep interview of 10 questions for 207 people involved per year, at least in the last 10 years.

articleTitle: Automatic evaluation of cracks with semantic segmentation model with U-Net and an Efficient Net-b2
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: The appearance of cracks in underground infrastructures when presenting gives meaning of weakening, Peru being a seismic country it’s crucial to have the capability to locate the cracks, because it could produce an irreparable problem. It proposes a semantic segmentation model with U-Net and an efficient Net-b2 process with visual evaluation to carry out a detection system without contact, more fast and provide greater safety to workers. The system is based on digital image processing because it is a modern technique that allows combining various techniques in order to identify a particular object, in addition to creating a database with the processed data for subsequent control or monitoring. Our findings are an accuracy of 98.3% between the images labeled as cracks and non-cracks, and it indicates 97.61% by using filtering process according to the morphological operations and surfaces, better results were obtained in extracting the edges of the cracks.

articleTitle: Adaptations of Neuroprostheses for Training: A Technological and Systematic Review
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: Certain medical conditions, genetic disabilities, and/or accidents limit certain parts of the body, such as the upper and/or lower extremities. This has seen technological advancement and has provided the development of various robotic devices (Neuroprosthetics) to assist in the rehabilitation process. Likewise, the use of Neural Networks, Supervised Machine Learning, or motion testing has the purpose of training the device itself to connect through sensors that capture biological signals to be pre-processed in controllers to target the movement to be performed. This research aims to analyze the characteristics of the components, control, and type of training for developing an efficient Neuroprosthesis. As a result of this research, different databases and search engines were used to collect information from various research from 2020 to 2023. Finally, it is concluded that the study aims to provide the most relevant information possible in the field of Neuroprosthesis concerning its training to be used in future research works and to be able to build and/or adapt a device with better characteristics for daily activities of the user and in the rehabilitation process.

articleTitle: Evaluation of fruit selection with ensemble model in the Peruvian industry
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: This paper allows to evaluate fruits with the ensemble algorithm with artificial vision, besides, it evaluates the systematic review with the PRISMA methodology thought the last 10 years. Our findings are the application of TensorFlow and self-supervised multi-network fusion classification models. Some researchers describe classification errors. The deep learning methodology is also an efficient way of classifying and applying algorithms that optimally analyze features such as color, shape, and texture of the object. On the other hand, we can implement artificial intelligence to this work since in recent years it has been developing in all industrial sectors and is bringing positive results. Finally, it uses a case study with the limitations to admit safe practices in a company dedicated to agricultural production and also over time that when studying the last cycle and at the same time working, the availability of time is limited to be able to use it in a work area. The results are an mean absolute error for size evaluation of 92.92%, color evaluation with 93.23%, and the assessment of the maturity, defects and quality of 97.72% after the evaluation of 1271 research articles with the systematic review process.

articleTitle: An Open Hardware Bioprinter Part I: A bioextruder with a peristaltic pump approach
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: This study presents the development and characterization of an open source bioextruder for 3D bioprinting, focusing on its application in research laboratories in South America. Bioextruder design is based on several requirements, the design was manufactured using techniques of 3D printing and its electronic control is managed using an Arduino Mega and Ramps 1.4 shield. The paper evaluates mechanical and biological properties, demonstrating that the flow behavior of alginate through the bioextruder is influenced by its concentration, viscosity, and extrusion rate. Results: As for the mechanical characterization test, for low alginate concentrations high velocities show stable extrusion values, while for high concentrations, a low velocity gives stable results. Strand thickness consistent results were obtained with respect to the width of the prints. It is also shown that cell viability decreases as the extrusion speed increases. Conclusion: This research demonstrates a successful bioextruder for precise 3D bioprinting, emphasizing open-source hardware’s significance particularly in resource-limited regions like Latin America.

articleTitle: Implementation of a Web System Using the Design Thinking Methodology to Enhance Administrative Management at Centro de Investigación, Innovación y Desarrollo del Aprendizaje (CIIDEA) in 2023
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: Administrative management in educational centers in Ecuador and Colombia faces challenges in aligning with regulations and the non-use of digital tools. In Peru, the COVID-19 pandemic has further exacerbated these issues, making it difficult for educational centers to transition to digital technologies. However, this research aims to improve administrative management at the Center for Research, Innovation and Development of Learning (CIIDEA), an institution that offers graduate programs for educators and has problems adapting to digital tools. The user-centered development methodology used is Design Thinking and involves five phases: empathize, define, ideate, prototype, and test. The results, based on the administrative management indicators used in this study, show that the resource planning compliance rate improved by 38.15%, the efficiency in the allocation of financial resources improved from 0 to 91.62% and the student cost decreased from S/. 35.50 to S/. 24.61 (Peruvian sol currency). These results demonstrate improvements in resource planning compliance rate, financial resource allocation efficiency, and student costs, indicating that developing a project focused on information technologies and user-centered is both feasible and enhances the user experience. Finally, the project’s success is attributed to the positive user experience of those using the implemented technological solutions.

articleTitle: Method Based on Genetic Algorithms for the Optimization of the Number of Luminaires in Apartment Buildings According to Peruvian Regulations and the Total Power Consumed
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: Among the objectives sought to be achieved in the country’s 2050 national agenda is the development of innovations that contribute to energy sustainability and savings in electricity consumption. This research aims to summarize this goal. A method based on genetic algorithms has been developed that allows calculating the number of optimal luminaires, their price and the total electrical power consumed, improving energy efficiency and lighting comfort inside buildings following the electrical installations section of the National Regulations. Peruvian Buildings (RNE). The investigation is divided into two parts. In the first part, a state of the art was carried out that shows the main contributions in research on energy sustainability and background on the calculation of indoor luminaires. In the second, a method based on genetic algorithms is shown, an artificial intelligence algorithm that seeks to optimize the calculation of luminaires. The results confirm optimal efficiency in electrical consumption and energy savings in interior lighting.

articleTitle: Medical Bio-Modeling: A First Report on the Implementation of 3D Printing for Congenital Anomalies in Peru.
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: Congenital anomalies are among the leading causes of mortality worldwide, predominantly affecting lower-middle-income countries. Furthermore, these complex and rare anatomical structures are sometimes not fully comprehensible until the surgical procedure begins. To address these challenges, increased innovation and new procedures are needed, as multiple factors hinder the advancement of neonatal surgery in our country. Obtaining clinical models represented in three dimensions (3D) can provide additional details and hands-on surgical training for medical doctors, thereby reducing the risks associated with these surgeries. Clinical models have already demonstrated success as a potential supplementary technique for medical imaging. However, the existing infrastructure and local resources present significant challenges. Therefore, an in-house 3D printing fabrication procedure must be made available. In this retrospective study, we are combining image computing software and 3D printing technology to create, for the first time, five biomodels of patients with congenital anomalies in a real clinical setting in a middle-income country like Peru. The evidence obtained will contribute to the incorporation of 3D printing in the field of diagnosis and treatment at one of Peru's most critical public children's hospitals. This breakthrough opens the door for future developments and the integration of these facilities into more public institutions.

articleTitle: Model-Free ANN-based control for Three-Phase Induction Motor Speed Control
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: The speed control of Induction Motors (IMs) is one of the most complex control problems, and is an active research topic in the control field. In this research work, a neural controller is proposed to address this problem. Our proposal uses an artificial neural network (ANN) with an online learning algorithm. Moreover, we developed a modified version of the Adam optimization algorithm to train the ANN online. Experimental results on a Three-Phase IM test bench show that the ANN-based controller is able to learn in real-time and it outperforms the widely used proportional integral (PI) controller.

articleTitle: Datalogger for Low-Cost High Mountain Weather Stations: Design, Optimization and Testing of Power Consumption and Compatibility with Satellite Transmitter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: This paper presents the design, optimization, and laboratory testing of a low-cost Datalogger for meteorological stations in high mountain environments. The lack of meteorological data in the high Andean basins hinders natural resource management and disaster prevention, therefore Low-Cost Weather Stations are presented as efficient solutions to collect such data and meet the demand for research in these areas. The Datalogger based on a ESP32 microcontroller was developed to capture, store, and transmit meteorological data, while also addressing the challenges of operating in remote and harsh conditions. The study focused on integrating essential functionalities, such as data transmission, with a strong emphasis on satellite communication for global coverage this by means of electronic components to obtain an RS485 output interface. The optimization process involved state-of-the-art review, careful selection of components and PCB design. Two versions of the Datalogger were fabricated and subjected to laboratory testing to assess their performance and reliability. The results showed that both versions exhibited satisfactory responses in terms of data acquisition, communication interfaces, and sensor integration. Overall, the Datalogger demonstrated promising results, showcasing its potential for scientific research and environmental monitoring in challenging high mountain environments. Future work will involve field testing to validate its performance under real-world conditions and further refine the design for optimal functionality.

articleTitle: Characterization and differentiation of electromyographic signals acquired with the BITalino platform in Peruvian university students
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: This study aims to characterize and differentiate electromyographic (EMG) signals acquired using the BITalino platform in Peruvian university females. Electromyography (EMG) is a diagnostic procedure that records the electrical activity of motor units near the electrode placement area. EMG has various applications, from assessing neuromuscular health in pathologies to controlling prosthetics and exoskeletons. The study focuses on the BITalino (r)evolution kit, a user-friendly option that facilitates rapid data processing. Despite its numerous applications for surface EMG (sEMG), consistent processing criteria are lacking, especially when comparing pathological and healthy cases. The research aims to evaluate and characterize the electromyographic response using the BITalino kit to measure muscle action potential in university females during an exertion exercise. The study follows an experimental design, considering various aspects such as subject selection, comparison groups, measurement procedures, and data analysis.

articleTitle: SafeSteps: A mobile app for monitoring and tracking the elderly with Alzheimer's using an IoT device
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: A considerable population of older adults in Peru suffers from Alzheimer's disease, which causes progressive degradation of cognitive abilities, high dependency, and other symptoms that result in reduced quality of life. Additionally, memory loss and disorientation account for half of the cases of disappearance of older adults, especially when family members do not have the time or resources to provide care for the elderly. Therefore, an IoT architecture and a real-time monitoring and control system for older adults with Alzheimer's disease is proposed, using an IoT device connected to the mobile devices of family members or caregivers. The proposed system was implemented in five layers: capture, communication, business logic, storage, and presentation. It consists of two applications: a smartwatch and a smartphone. Validation tests were conducted with caregivers and health experts in various districts of Lima Metropolitana, Peru. The results demonstrate that the proposal has high accuracy (100%) and a fast response time (5.6 s) for notifying the caregiver of exceeded limits. The survey results from health experts and caregivers showed an average rating of 4.6 (Completely agree), 4.4 (Agree), and 4.6 (Completely agree) in terms of "functionality," "efficiency," and "usability," respectively.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of an Inspection Robot for Crack Detection in Flooded Pipes
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: The pipeline used to supply drinking water to Andean communities is a crucial component of the water management project in mining complexes that aims to preserve local resources. However, the degraded state of the pipeline poses significant environmental, social and economic risks. To overcome these challenges, the present work proposes the development of a teleoperated robot for the inspection of flooded pipelines. The vehicle features an IP68 protection system to ensure underwater operation, along with measurement and analysis capabilities to assess the pipeline profile. In addition, it incorporates real-time video transmission and visual inspection aids through a graphical interface. Effective communication is ensured within a distance of 600 meters between the vehicle and the command post with a latency of less than 100 ms. Furthermore, an important aspect of this work is the successful segmentation of cracks and fissures using a hybrid CNN-RNN architecture, trained on a dataset comprising online repository images and images captured inside the pipeline.

articleTitle: A Review on Mobile Robots and its Design Requirements to Clean Solar Photovoltaic Modules
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: Solar photovoltaic energy has experienced growing interest as a renewable and sustainable source in contrast to conventional fossil fuel-based energy. Households, businesses and government institutions have invested in the installation of solar PV panels due to their smaller footprint and the significant savings in electricity consumption they offer. Despite the benefits of solar PV, the accumulation of dirt on the glass surface of solar panels, such as dust and other contaminants, reduces their efficiency by obstructing the amount of sunlight reaching the PV cells, affecting their power generation capacity by 20% and damaging the cells or shortening their lifetime. Therefore, maintenance and cleaning of solar panels is crucial to avoid future problems and to ensure efficient production of electrical energy. This is why different researchers and companies continue to search for new ways of cleaning PV modules. Since the nature of this task is costly and high-risk, specialised services are required for monitoring and cleaning solar photovoltaic panels. In this context, specialised mobile robots have been developed, which perform cleaning and analysis of solar panels in an automated way. This review focuses on analysing and comparing various mobile robots used for automated solar panel cleaning, including their characteristics, advantages and limitations. The aim is to identify the most promising technologies and possible areas of improvement to encourage wider adoption of these automated systems in the maintenance of solar photovoltaic installations. Moreover, recommended design requirements for these type of robots are listed. By facilitating access to an efficient and low-cost cleaning service, it is expected that more households and businesses will be able to maintain their solar panels in adequate condition, thus ensuring a continuous and efficient production of electricity.

articleTitle: An Algorithm for Image Transmission Using FM-RDS Communication Modules
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to multi-band image transmission using the FM-RDS standard. An algorithm has been designed and implemented to enable efficient data packet transmission within the payload of the standard. To accomplish this, coding techniques have been employed to ensure viable time ranges, especially for potential applications in emergency alert monitoring. The test results demonstrate that a 512 x 512 pixels RGB image can be transmitted in 109.06 seconds with a packet loss rate of less than 0.5%. In addition, a basic comparison was made with the LoRa link, revealing a better performance under the same experimental conditions.

articleTitle: An autonomous navigation system for an unmanned surface vehicle for plastic waste collection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: This article proposes the design of an autonomous navigation system intended for Unmanned Surface Vehicles (USVs) in the form of catamarans with differential propulsion, whose primary function is the collection of plastic waste in aquatic environments such as seas and lakes. The fundamental goal of this system is to optimize the operational capabilities of the USVs by increasing their navigational autonomy, consequently reducing the costs associated with their operation and production. In this context, the vehicle has been mathematically modeled, and a navigation system composed of four essential components has been established. The first component involves heading control, which utilizes GPS and IMU to estimate the orientation of the USV. The second component is the obstacle avoidance system, which employs a lidar sensor. The third component is a collection system that relies on a computer vision model with convolutional neural networks to detect different types of plastics and manage the collection process. Finally, an architecture has been designed to facilitate the interconnection of all the aforementioned control systems.

articleTitle: Internal positioning system for trajectory control of mobile robots
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: The current and well-known positioning systems such as GPS do not function properly in indoor spaces, as the surrounding structure prevents satellite signals from penetrating and locating a target. The purpose of this article is to develop an alternative solution for positioning mobile robots or specific targets in enclosed spaces. The aim of its development is to enable its application in service robotics within facilities such as offices, laboratories, hospitals, warehouses, homes, etc., whether using ground-based or aerial robots. The development of an indoor positioning system based on the concept of intelligent spaces is proposed. A detection and monitoring system is developed, a system for converting 2D to 3D spaces. Obtaining the position of an object in space through a marker. Finally, the testing and validation of the system is carried out in an environment within the laboratory. It is possible to develop an intelligent system capable of detecting objects in space through markers and reconstructing their trajectory. The developed system opens the way to biomechanical studies using motion capture, development of trajectory control systems, geomorphological reconstruction, scanning of mechanical parts or biomechanical parts, etc.

articleTitle: An information supply chain allowing data analytics for the network of weather stations Niño 5
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: Data analytics is providing benefits in different areas by generating value for organisations. The analysis of meteorological data is an area in which descriptive and predictive analytics can deliver high value to understand climate events better and use the information for different purposes like disaster prevention, climate change management, climate events prediction, increasing efficiency in economic sectors like fishing and agroindustry, and so on. This paper reports on the design, implementation and validation of the information supply chain (ISC) allowing data analytics for the network of weather stations Niño 5. The proposed ISC includes the data sources definition, the identification of the information recipients, the data acquisition and preparation for data analytics, and the design and validation of dashboards for descriptive analytics. The proposal is implemented using Tableau Desktop, Tableau Prep Builder and Tableau Online (Tableau Cloud). The proposal validation is done with stakeholders based on the importance of the Network Niño 5 in the study of the El Nino-Southern Oscillation, which has a relevant social impact and affects several economic sectors in South America. The results are promising and define the path to enhancing data analytics processes based on the data collected by the Network Niño 5.

articleTitle: External Noise Canceling Analysis for an Urban Environment in Lima
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: Lima faces a significant problem with noise pollution, especially in urban areas. The urban population has increased in recent years, contributing to the problem. The World Health Organization recommends lower noise levels to protect human health. Traffic and industrial activities are the predominant sources of noise pollution in Lima. Traffic noise can reach up to 85 decibels, especially during rush hours, while industrial activity produces noise levels of up to 75 decibels, posing health risks to residents and workers. If the problem of noise pollution is not addressed, people exposed to high noise levels will suffer significant hearing damage in the future. However, technological advances offer potential solutions, and noise reduction methods, including noise cancellation devices, can play a crucial role. This work aims to analyze the three most commonly used algorithms: Least Mean Square (LMS), Normalised Least Mean Square (NLMS), and Recursive Least Square (RLS) for noise reduction in an urban environment. We analyzed the performance of these algorithms in five different locations in Lima. It is possible to reduce the noise in different scenarios, with NLMS being optimal. Noise reduction analysis allows future applications in physical IoT devices. They reduce noise for the well-being of users.

articleTitle: Approach for Personalized Recommendations to Enhance Customer Service Process in Peruvian Restaurants using OpenAI Contextual Chatbot
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: In the current digital era, efficiently accessing relevant information is crucial for various applications such as restaurant recommendation systems, website searches, book recommendations, among others. This study presents an approach for personalized recommendations in improving the customer service process in restaurants using OpenAI's Contextual Chatbot. The approach consists of six phases: (1) Data preprocessing, (2) Embedding and storage, (3) Scheduled updating, (4) Document retrieval, (5) Context adaptation and request creation, and (6) Response generation. OpenAI's text embeddings are used to convert application data into vectors and store them in a vector database. These vectors are used to retrieve similar records and generate contextualized responses using the GPT-3.5 model. The chatbot's performance is evaluated in terms of accuracy and user satisfaction. Two scenarios were used in the experimentation: (a) with the proposed solution and (b) without the solution. The results demonstrated an operational efficiency of 86.67% with the proposed solution and the versatility of the proposed methodology, showcasing its potential for application in a wide range of domains, including websites, books, PDFs, and other forms of documentation.

articleTitle: A Characteristic Surface Generated by Multivariate Kernel Regression for Assessing Wave Power in the Peru Basin
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE XXX International Conference on Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computing (INTERCON)
abstract: The Peru Basin is an unexplored source of clean energy. Projects to install wave farms in this region depend on assessing the energy power that this domain can offer. The state-of-the-art indicates that the technology for this evaluation has been developed for ocean conditions belonging to the Northern Hemisphere of the Earth. Those conditions are far from the local ocean conditions of the Peru Basin, characterised to be an open sea. Consequently, that technology is not proper for wave power evaluation of the Peru Basin.
